resources.string: Couldn’t save on this phone. Try again.
Getting the scanner ready. This needs Google Play services and can take a moment the first time.
The server asked to wait %1$d seconds before retrying.
Allow the camera to scan QR codes
The camera is only used to read QR codes. Nothing is recorded or uploaded.
Camera access is turned off for this app. Turn it on in the app’s settings, or type the code instead.
Use the QR marked “OEM / Pre-Authorized — Internal Only” on the Portal’s Product ID sheet. It holds the Caller ID and API key.
The Caller must be active and assigned to the Hall whose tickets you test.
An API key is exactly 64 characters, 0–9 and a–f.
The API key is stored encrypted on this phone and is never shown in full.
That’s a customer ticket. Scan the Caller label (the OEM / Pre-Authorized QR).
That QR isn’t a Caller label.
The label’s Caller ID isn’t valid.
The label’s API key isn’t valid.
Choose a Portal server in Settings first.
Caller ID and API key are valid
This confirms an active Caller. Redeeming also needs the Caller to be assigned to a Hall.
The server didn’t accept these details
Check the Caller ID and API key, and that the Caller is active in the Portal.
This server can’t check Caller details
The Portal has no verify-credentials endpoint. You can still save the Caller and redeem.
Too many checks. Wait a minute and try again.
Point the camera at a ticket QR
That QR isn’t a Bingo ticket.
That’s a Caller label. To change the Caller, use Settings.
The server may have accepted it. Retry it with the same request ID from the history.
Paste or type the whole code. It starts with BC1. and ends with 64 letters and digits.
That isn’t a valid BC1 ticket code.
This isn’t a valid ticket code.
The Caller or server has changed
This request was sent to %1$s as Caller %2$s. To retry or test it, switch back to them in Settings, or start over with a new request.
Not sent: the Caller or server changed since this request was first sent.
The app stopped before the server answered. Retry it with the same request ID; the server returns the saved result if it was accepted.
Sent exactly as typed. Case and spaces count.
Locked: this request was sent from this tablet ID.
Too long: %1$d bytes. The limit is %2$d.
Control characters such as line breaks aren’t allowed.
This text can’t be sent as UTF-8.
A retry must reuse this ID. A new scan of a ticket gets a new one.
No Caller is set. Add one in Settings.
No Portal server is set. Choose one in Settings.
Sends this request ID again from a different tablet ID. The server must refuse it without revealing the original result.
Use a different tablet ID from the one that sent the request.
the saved result, recovered, nothing added
The ticket is now redeemed onto this tablet ID. “Redeemed” doesn’t mean cards were loaded.
The server recognised this request and returned its saved result. Nothing was added. A tablet must not load the same redemption ID twice.
Cards are loaded by Portal Game Type ID. Names are for display only and can change if a Game Type is renamed. Paper is never included.
The server sent HTTP %1$d, but the contract says %2$d for this code.
Redemption ID is a lowercase UUID v4
State is “redeemed” and recovered is true or false
Session details are complete and valid
Package details are complete and valid
Game Types are unique with positive faces
The Portal refused the request format. Check that the server address points to a Portal with the redemption relay.
The server didn’t accept the ticket code format.
The Portal didn’t accept the Caller ID and API key. Check the Caller in Settings, and that it is active in the Portal.
The Caller isn’t active, or isn’t assigned to a Hall.
This ticket was sold by another Hall, not the Caller’s Hall. Nothing was redeemed in either Hall.
No active ticket matches this code in the Caller’s Hall.
This ticket was already accepted. A new scan with a new request ID is always refused, even on the same tablet. Only the original request ID gets the saved result.
This request ID was already used for a different ticket or tablet. The original result isn’t revealed.
The ticket belongs to a different dated Session.
This ticket would take this tablet over the electronic-card limit for at least one Game Type in this Session. Nothing was added. Another tablet has its own allowance.
The ticket was refunded or cancelled. Earlier accepted history stays, but the ticket can’t be used.
The saved purchase details for this ticket are invalid. Staff need to review the order.
A Caller can send 15 requests a minute, shared with its other traffic. Wait, then retry with the same request ID.
The ticket’s Game Type mapping isn’t available. Retry with the same request ID once it is restored.
The server couldn’t verify the ticket. Retry with the same request ID.
The server couldn’t confirm whether the redemption was saved. Retry with the same request ID, never a new one, to find out.
The server sent an error code that isn’t in the contract.
Plain HTTP is blocked in this build
The server may have accepted the ticket. Retry with the same request ID to find out. A new ID would be refused as already redeemed.
The request didn’t reach the server, so nothing changed. Check the connection and the server address, then try again.
The server didn’t answer with JSON, for example an HTML error page from a proxy or web server.
The server answered 200, but the body doesn’t match the redemption contract.
The error body doesn’t match the contract’s error format.
The server redirected the request. Redirects aren’t followed, so use the final address in Settings.
The answer was larger than the contract allows.
This deletes every saved attempt on this phone, including unconfirmed ones you might need to retry. Nothing changes on the server.
Every request you send is listed here, so you can open it and retry it with the same request ID.
No server is active. Save a custom address or choose Staging.
The Portal’s address, starting with https://
Starts with https://, or http:// for a local Portal in this debug build
Plain http:// is only allowed in debug builds. Use https://.
Remove the user name or password from the address.
Remove the ? or # part from the address.
Each physical tablet needs its own ID within a Hall. The electronic-card limit is counted per tablet, per dated Session and Game Type.
The Caller ID and API key are deleted from this phone. You’ll need to scan the Caller label again. The history stays.

Tests the Bingo Portal Caller redemption relay (POST /api/caller/redemptions, contract version 1). It sends exactly what a Caller sends for a player tablet and shows what came back. It never loads cards or games.
